```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)
```

A predicted mean is a linear combination of the model's coefficients. When some
treatment combinations have no data, or two factors are confounded, some of these
combinations cannot be estimated from the data: emmeans prints them as `nonEst` and SAS
as `Non-est`. This vignette shows what predictmeans does in these cases and how to get
means and comparisons that are estimable.

In short:

- **Cell means** of combinations with no data are not shown.
- **A mean that averages over an empty cell** (e.g. the mean of a nitrogen level over
  the varieties when one variety lacks that level) keeps the rule of predictmeans 1.x:
  it is the average of the observed cells, with a warning naming it.
- **Its comparisons** with other means are made on the cells both means have (column
  `over` of `pairs`), not as the difference of two averages over different cells.
- **Means that the data cannot determine** (because factors are confounded) are `NA`,
  with a message. Their pairwise differences are still given when they can be
  estimated, and letters are given among those.
- The `means` table has an `estimable` column and the number of observations, `n`.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(predictmeans)
```

## An empty cell

Suppose the plots of Victory at the highest nitrogen level were lost in the oats split
plot:

```{r}
Oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
Oats$N <- factor(Oats$nitro)
Om <- subset(Oats, !(Variety == "Victory" & N == "0.6"))
with(Om, table(Variety, N))
fm <- lmer(yield ~ N * Variety + (1 | Block/Variety), data = Om)
```

The model with the interaction has one coefficient fewer (lme4 drops it). The cell means
are those of the 11 combinations with data:

```{r, warning = FALSE}
pm_cells <- predictmeans(fm, "N:Variety", plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)
nrow(pm_cells$means)
```

The nitrogen means average over the varieties. For N = 0.6 only two varieties have data,
so its mean is their average, and predictmeans warns:

```{r}
pm_n <- predictmeans(fm, "N", plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)
pm_n$means[, c("N", "estimate", "std.error", "n")]
```

That mean leaves out Victory, the lowest-yielding variety at the other nitrogen levels,
so it is too high compared with the others; emmeans calls it non-estimable. The
difference 125.8 − 79.4 = 46.4 would mix the nitrogen effect with the variety effect
(Victory is in the mean of N = 0 but not in that of 0.6). So predictmeans compares N = 0.6
with each other level on the varieties both have, Golden Rain and Marvellous (column
`over`): 0.6 − 0 is the average of their two differences, 42.5. Pairs among the complete
levels are the differences of the means as usual:

```{r}
pm_n2 <- suppressWarnings(predictmeans(fm, "N", pairwise = TRUE, plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE))
pm_n2$pairs[, c("level1", "level2", "over", "estimate", "std.error", "p.value")]
```

Comparing the two averages instead would wrongly call 0.6 and 0.4 different here (p = 0.03
against 0.08 on the common varieties). In simulations (`dev/review-defaults.md` in the
package sources) comparing averages over different cells rejected 8–78% of true null
hypotheses when the other factor had an effect; comparing on the common cells 4–6%. When
two means have no cell in common their difference is NA (`over = "none"`). `pm_joint()`
tests a term on the cells common to all its means, and `contrastmeans()` compares on the
cells the means of each contrast have in common.

Other comparisons that stay within the observed cells are sound too, e.g. nitrogen levels
within each variety:

```{r, warning = FALSE}
pm_v <- predictmeans(fm, "N:Variety", atvar = "Variety", adj = "tukey", plot = FALSE,
                     prtnum = FALSE)
within <- subset(pm_v$pairs, !is.na(by))
head(within[, c("level1", "level2", "by", "estimate", "p.adj")])
```

or contrasts written with `specify_contrast()`, which refuses means that cannot be
estimated:

```{r, warning = FALSE}
cm <- specify_contrast(Kmatrix(fm, "N:Variety"),
  N_effect_GR_and_M = (`0.6:Golden Rain` + `0.6:Marvellous`)/2 - (`0:Golden Rain` + `0:Marvellous`)/2)
contrastmeans(fm, "N:Variety", ctrmatrix = cm)[[1]]
```

## Confounded factors

In this spray trial the highest spray volume was used only with fine droplets, and the
other two volumes only with medium droplets:

```{r}
set.seed(3)
spray <- data.frame(
  droplet = factor(rep(c("medium", "fine"), c(40, 10)), levels = c("medium", "fine")),
  vol = factor(c(rep(c("130", "200"), 20), rep("400", 10))),
  conc = factor(rep(c("none", "half"), 25)))
spray$y <- 5 + 0.3 * (spray$conc == "half") - 0.4 * (spray$droplet == "fine") +
  rnorm(50, sd = 0.2)
with(spray, table(droplet, vol))
```

In a model with `droplet` and `vol` as separate factors, the effect of volume 400 cannot
be told apart from that of fine droplets. A volume mean averaged over both droplet sizes
needs both, so none of the volume means can be estimated:

```{r}
fs <- lm(y ~ droplet + conc + vol, data = spray)
pv <- predictmeans(fs, "vol", pairwise = TRUE, plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)
pv$means[, c("vol", "estimate", "n", "estimable", "group")]
pv$pairs[, c("level1", "level2", "estimate", "std.error", "p.value")]
```

The difference between volumes 130 and 200 (both with medium droplets) can still be
estimated, and the letters compare those two only.

There are two ways to get means. `weights = "cells"` averages over the observed
combinations only, weighting them by their numbers of observations; these means depend on
how the data happen to be spread over the other factors:

```{r}
predictmeans(fs, "vol", weights = "cells", plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)$means[, c("vol", "estimate", "std.error")]
```

Better, state the structure in the model: volume is nested in droplet size. The means of
the observed droplet–volume combinations, averaged equally over `conc`, are then
estimable (and equal to what emmeans gives after detecting the nesting):

```{r}
fs2 <- lm(y ~ conc + droplet/vol, data = spray)
pn <- predictmeans(fs2, "droplet:vol", pairwise = TRUE, plot = FALSE, prtnum = FALSE)
pn$means[, c("droplet", "vol", "estimate", "std.error", "n", "group")]
```

The warning about missing combinations refers to the three combinations that cannot
occur in this design.

## Checklist

- Look at the `n` and `estimable` columns of the `means` table, and at warnings and
  messages.
- Compare means that average over the same cells; use `atvar` or contrasts within the
  observed cells when some are empty.
- When factors are confounded, write the structure into the model (nesting, or one
  factor for the observed combinations) rather than averaging over combinations that
  do not exist.
